output.question: I want a custom Signal that tags agent answers requiring human review. How do I create it in the Weave UI?

task_plan.description: Explain how to create a custom Signal in the Weave UI that tags agent answers requiring human review.
task_plan.request_quote: I want a custom Signal that tags agent answers requiring human review. How do I create it in the Weave UI?

outcome_assessments.answer_quote: Create it as a custom tag signal from the Signals tab of the Agents view.
outcome_assessments.reason: Gives documented UI steps and fields, framing the human-review wording as a suggestion.

output.answer:
Create it as a custom tag signal from the Signals tab of the Agents view. You write a **Definition** prompt describing "needs human review", and Weave uses an LLM judge to tag matching agent turns [S1][S2].

**Steps**
1. In Forge, select your project [S1].
2. In the Weave project sidebar, click **Agents**, then click the **Signals** tab [S1].
3. Click **+ Create your first signal** or **New signal**, then click **Custom Signal** in the drawer [S1].
4. In the **Custom tags** drawer, fill in these fields [S1]:
   - **Tag name**: the label shown in the Agents view. For example, you could use something like "Needs human review". That wording is my suggestion, not from the docs.
   - **Definition**: a prompt describing the behavior to detect. Weave sends it to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches. Write your review criteria here. For example, you might describe answers that are uncertain, risky, or unsupported. The docs' own example is "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   - **Scorer name**: the name of the underlying scorer object.
   - **Inference model or custom runtime**: the model that scores turns. Serverless Inference is the default and consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
5. Optionally, change these settings [S1]:
   - **+ Add tag** defines another tag on the same signal.
   - Under **Advanced**, **Include tool calls** adds the turn's tool calls to the context sent to the scoring model.
   - Under **Advanced**, **Only score turns matching** limits scoring by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave it empty to score every turn, and multiple filters are combined with `AND`.
   - Under **Advanced**, **Sample rate** sets the fraction of matching turns that are scored. Lowering it reduces cost on high-traffic agents.
6. Click **Create signal** [S1].

After you create it, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab [S1].

Signals score agent *turns* [S2], so the tag applies to turns rather than to separate answer objects. The docs I read don't show a specific "human review" template, so the Definition wording is yours to write.

sources.title: Create a custom signal
sources.heading: Create a custom tag signal
sources.text:
## Create a custom tag signal

To create a custom tag signal:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.

2. In the **Weave project sidebar**, click **Agents**.

3. In the tab bar, click **Signals**.

4. On the Signals tab, click **+ Create your first signal**, or **New signal**.

5. In the drawer, click **Custom Signal**.

   ![The Custom tags drawer with Tag name, Definition, Scorer name, and Inference model fields for creating a custom signal.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/custom-signal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=b01a4b83a0ef2c7717d78efc406a1de0)

6. In the **Custom tags** drawer, configure the following fields:
   * **Tag name**: The label that appears in the Agents view for the behavior you want to monitor.
   * **Definition**: A prompt that describes the behavior you want the signal to detect. Weave sends this prompt to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches the behavior. For example, to catch a specific product failure: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   * **+ Add tag** (Optional): Click to define another tag on the same signal. For example, if you support multiple products, add a separate tag for each product so you can track frustration per product instead of only in aggregate.
   * **Scorer name**: The name for the underlying scorer object.
   * **Inference model or custom runtime**: The model used to score matching turns. [Serverless Inference](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless.md) is the default. CoreWeave Serverless Inference consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
   * **Include tool calls** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then check the box to include the turn's tool calls in the context sent to the scoring model.
   * **Only score turns matching** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then add one or more filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave empty to score every agent turn. Weave combines multiple filters with `AND` logic.
   * **Sample rate** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then set the fraction of matching agent turns the signal scores. For high-traffic agents, lower the sample rate to score a fraction of matching turns instead of every turn and reduce cost.

7. In the **Custom tags** drawer, click **Create signal**.

After you create the signal, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab.
sources.page_context:
# Create a custom signal

> Create a custom Weave signal to tag agent turns for a behavior you define.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tags/create-tag.md).

A custom signal scores agent turns against a behavior you define, then shows that result as a tag in the [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-activity.md). Weave also provides [built-in signals](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md) for common cases, such as user frustration and jailbreaking. When those built-in signals don't cover what you want to monitor, create a custom signal. This page shows you how to create that custom tag signal in the Weights & Biases UI.

results.heading: Add a signal from the Monitors page
results.snippet:
## Add a signal from the Monitors page

Adding a signal turns on automated scoring so that Weave evaluates new production traces against that signal's criteria. To enable signals:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and then open your Weave project.
2. In the Weave project sidebar, select **Monitors**.
3. To add a signal to a project with no Monitors enabled, click on its card to activate its checkbox, then click **Setup monitors**.
4. To add signals to an existing Monitor, select **Browse signals** at the top-right on the **Monitors** page. This opens the **Add signals** drawer, which lists available signals grouped by category (such as Quality classifiers and Error classifiers), each with a checkbox. You can select individual signals, use **Enable all** for a group, or select **Create custom signal**. Then select **Add signals** at the bottom of the drawer.

After you add signals, Weave automatically scores incoming traces.

### See tagged Call traces on the Traces page

If you trace individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, Weave stores signal results as feedback on the Call object. You can query these results from the **Traces** page.

You can scan your traces for certain behavior in the **Traces** page using the **Signals** column. The Signals column shows tags when their criteria are met. Hover over these tags to see the confidence in the score and the reasoning.

![Weave Traces view with hover over of a Signals tag in the Signals column showing confidence and reasoning.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/weave_signals_trace_hover.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=bf7b8234b4a8a4584bb40e0a8af4b34b)

# Monitor your agents with signals

> Use Weave signals to score agent turns, apply tags, and surface quality and safety issues in production.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tags/create-tag.md).

The **Signals** tab shows tags and ratings for your agent's conversations. Use signals to automatically score the quality of your agent's responses, notice when a user is frustrated, or flag NSFW content.

results.snippet:
## Get started

To open the Agents view for your project:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.
2. In the sidebar menu, select **Agents** to view all agent conversations saved for your project.

The Agents view is organized into a row of tabs across the top: **Dashboard**, **Agents**, **Conversations**, **Spans**, and **Signals**. The **Dashboard** tab gives a project-wide overview of agent activity, while the other tabs let you drill into individual agents, conversations, spans, and signals.

result.text:
## Create a custom tag signal

To create a custom tag signal:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.

2. In the **Weave project sidebar**, click **Agents**.

3. In the tab bar, click **Signals**.

4. On the Signals tab, click **+ Create your first signal**, or **New signal**.

5. In the drawer, click **Custom Signal**.

   ![The Custom tags drawer with Tag name, Definition, Scorer name, and Inference model fields for creating a custom signal.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/custom-signal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=b01a4b83a0ef2c7717d78efc406a1de0)

6. In the **Custom tags** drawer, configure the following fields:
   * **Tag name**: The label that appears in the Agents view for the behavior you want to monitor.
   * **Definition**: A prompt that describes the behavior you want the signal to detect. Weave sends this prompt to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches the behavior. For example, to catch a specific product failure: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   * **+ Add tag** (Optional): Click to define another tag on the same signal. For example, if you support multiple products, add a separate tag for each product so you can track frustration per product instead of only in aggregate.
   * **Scorer name**: The name for the underlying scorer object.
   * **Inference model or custom runtime**: The model used to score matching turns. [Serverless Inference](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless.md) is the default. CoreWeave Serverless Inference consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
   * **Include tool calls** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then check the box to include the turn's tool calls in the context sent to the scoring model.
   * **Only score turns matching** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then add one or more filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave empty to score every agent turn. Weave combines multiple filters with `AND` logic.
   * **Sample rate** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then set the fraction of matching agent turns the signal scores. For high-traffic agents, lower the sample rate to score a fraction of matching turns instead of every turn and reduce cost.

7. In the **Custom tags** drawer, click **Create signal**.

After you create the signal, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab.

# Create a custom signal

> Create a custom Weave signal to tag agent turns for a behavior you define.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tags/create-tag.md).

A custom signal scores agent turns against a behavior you define, then shows that result as a tag in the [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-activity.md). Weave also provides [built-in signals](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md) for common cases, such as user frustration and jailbreaking. When those built-in signals don't cover what you want to monitor, create a custom signal. This page shows you how to create that custom tag signal in the Weights & Biases UI.

Create it as a custom tag signal from the Signals tab of the Agents view. You write a **Definition** prompt describing "needs human review", and Weave uses an LLM judge to tag matching agent turns [S1][S2].

**Steps**
1. In Forge, select your project [S1].
2. In the Weave project sidebar, click **Agents**, then click the **Signals** tab [S1].
3. Click **+ Create your first signal** or **New signal**, then click **Custom Signal** in the drawer [S1].
4. In the **Custom tags** drawer, fill in these fields [S1]:
   - **Tag name**: the label shown in the Agents view. For example, you could use something like "Needs human review". That wording is my suggestion, not from the docs.
   - **Definition**: a prompt describing the behavior to detect. Weave sends it to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches. Write your review criteria here. For example, you might describe answers that are uncertain, risky, or unsupported. The docs' own example is "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   - **Scorer name**: the name of the underlying scorer object.
   - **Inference model or custom runtime**: the model that scores turns. Serverless Inference is the default and consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
5. Optionally, change these settings [S1]:
   - **+ Add tag** defines another tag on the same signal.
   - Under **Advanced**, **Include tool calls** adds the turn's tool calls to the context sent to the scoring model.
   - Under **Advanced**, **Only score turns matching** limits scoring by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave it empty to score every turn, and multiple filters are combined with `AND`.
   - Under **Advanced**, **Sample rate** sets the fraction of matching turns that are scored. Lowering it reduces cost on high-traffic agents.
6. Click **Create signal** [S1].

After you create it, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab [S1].

Signals score agent *turns* [S2], so the tag applies to turns rather than to separate answer objects. The docs I read don't show a specific "human review" template, so the Definition wording is yours to write.
